```{=html}
<div class="c2-top">
<div class="lx-card lx-cap-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<p class="lx-case-q">A 300 MW data center asks to connect at Prairie Town. Recommend how much of it connects this year and what the Plains Grid should build so it stays adequate through a hard year, and say who pays.</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Hand in:</b> a plan link and a two-page study note with its sensitivity chart and a paragraph from M2's notebook (below the note).</li>
<li><b>From:</b> the <a href="sb2-grid-room.html">Grid Room</a>'s engine on the fictional Plains Grid, with 2025's hourly shapes, a peak-demand week and a low-wind winter week.</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> every check under the note is in place (the brief's 0.1 loss-of-load days a year, the chart and the notebook paragraph among them), and the self-check reaches Proficient on every competence.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About 180 minutes: 70 to build and test plans, 70 to write the note, 40 to check it.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Plus M2's notebook, about 45 minutes: run every cell. Its practice section is optional, about 90 minutes more.</p>
</div>
<div class="lx-card lx-real c2-realworld">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">In the real world</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:code"><p>A late grid connection costs the developer lost <span class="lx-term" data-term="margin">margin</span> and <span class="lx-term" data-term="carrying-cost">carrying costs</span>; ratepayers face utility carrying and <span class="lx-term" data-term="stranded-cost">stranding</span> costs; society bears <span class="lx-term" data-term="external-cost">external costs</span>.</p><p>The study keeps these present-value accounts separate.</p><p>Staged energization can recover a large share of that cost.</p><p>Ratepayer exposure depends strongly on large-load <span class="lx-term" data-term="tariff">tariff</span> design.</p><footer>Approved excerpt of: Li et al. (2026), accepted paper, 2026 North American Power Symposium (NAPS); DOI pending.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">The full case: <a href="cf7-cost-of-waiting.html">case file CF7</a>. This capstone asks the network and adequacy side of the same question.</p>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-datanote c2-note"><svg class="lx-ic" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="12" cy="12" r="8.5"/><path d="M12 11v5M12 8v.2"/></svg><ul>
<li><b>Illustrative:</b> the Plains Grid, its plants, links, outage rates and the uprate's cost; the large load is a load only, flat at its connected size.</li>
<li><b>Based on SPP:</b> 2025's hourly shapes for the year and the hard weeks; 2024's as well for the adequacy check (EIA-930).</li>
<li><b>Costs:</b> EIA's and NREL's values as yearly payments in 2025 dollars, within ranges you set (sources below).</li>
<li><b>Precomputed:</b> the year of each of the 128 plans on the grid, solved with this engine on 5 November 2026, each day's status kept. One day at a time and the adequacy check run live.</li>
<li><b>The grid:</b> half or all of the load, flexible or not, 0, 2, 4 or 6 new peakers, a battery or not, an uprate or not, a 150 or 250 MW reserve.</li>
<li><b>Reserve:</b> one region-wide total; the model does not check whether it can reach a zone after a disturbance. The adequacy check counts plants and links, not this reserve.</li>
</ul></div>
```

## Write your two-page study note
:::

```{=html}
<div id="c2-note" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- c2-note:start -->
<ol class="lx-rn-outline"><li><b>Title and plan link:</b> the plan's link from the bench, and the date</li><li><b>Recommendation:</b> Three or four sentences: how much connects, what to build, and why.</li><li><b>The plan:</b> each choice, with its unit</li><li><b>Results:</b> each result, with its unit and boundary</li><li><b>Assumptions:</b> one sentence each</li><li><b>Sensitivity:</b> how one result moves when one input changes, and whether the plan was held fixed</li><li><b>Who pays, and is it fair?:</b> Two or three sentences: the large load, other customers, and the rule you chose.</li><li><b>What could still go wrong:</b> Two or three sentences: what the model leaves out that could change your answer.</li><li><b>Three zones against one bus (M2's notebook):</b> One paragraph, after running M2's notebook: what three zones and two links change against its one bus (prices that part, uplift, who is short).</li><li><b>Limits of this analysis:</b> what the model leaves out</li></ol>
<!-- c2-note:end -->
</div>
</div>
```
